subject.title: Bound batch file read with size cap in config-set-input

question: Should `openclaw config set --batch-file` adopt 8 MiB as its supported maximum, use another explicitly supported limit, or preserve the current unbounded compatibility behavior?
rationale: The implementation fixes an unbounded user-controlled read, but selecting a new hard ceiling changes the existing CLI contract and cannot be derived safely from tests or the related hook-metadata precedent.

options.title: Confirm a documented batch-file maximum
options.body: Approve a specific supported capacity, including 8 MiB if intended, and merge with the current explicit error and boundary coverage.

options.title: Choose a different capacity
options.body: Set a maintainer-approved limit that reflects supported large configuration operations, then update the constant, error text, and boundary tests.

options.title: Preserve current compatibility for now
options.body: Do not merge a hard rejection until a compatible bounded-input design and public contract are agreed.

recommendation.title: Confirm a documented batch-file maximum
recommendation.body: Approve a specific supported capacity, including 8 MiB if intended, and merge with the current explicit error and boundary coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion explicitly asks this person to select the public capacity and compatibility direction.
